Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finsight.ai>

Subject: Strange output divergence when Redwood routes to variant B

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency looked great and the team is excited. We started a small load POC this morning and ran into a behavior that's blocking us from progressing to the next milestone.

Symptom: When FinSight sends the same request twice in succession, ~7% of the time the second response is semantically different (shorter, omits a key data extraction field) only after your system reroutes to a variant (you called it "variant-B") during sustained load. The first request returns the expected structured output.

I attached two artifacts: a trimmed request payload and a short log excerpt with request IDs. The earliest failing request id is rs-20261127-00123 (see perf-sample-logs.txt).

Questions for you and your engineering partners:
- Is there any SDK behavior we should be aware of that could cause state to leak between requests (we're using your Node SDK v0.9.2 with long polling enabled)?
- Can the runtime surface when a request was served by a fallback/variant model vs. the primary model? We need a deterministic way in our telemetry to correlate changes in outputs with a model variant event.

Can you triage with runtime and let us know what information you need from our side? We're happy to share live traces. We have a weekly sync on Tuesday; would prefer to resolve before then if possible.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of Data Products | FinSight Analytics

Initial notes:
- We don't expect any per-request state to persist between independent API calls. SDK long-polling shouldn't change model isolation, but there are a couple of historical edge cases around KV cache TTLs and prefix caching that can change behavior across requests if the runtime incorrectly matches cache keys.
- We can definitely emit a model_variant field in the response metadata on our side for diagnosis; I want to confirm the impact before we promise a permanent SDK change.

Karthik / Marissa — can you take a look at the attached sample request and rs-20261127-00123 log and confirm whether this looks like a cache key collision or a model fallback switch? Also advise whether we can add a non-breaking metadata field (model_variant, routed_from) in the short term for FinSight's telemetry.

Tom — I'll set up a short triage call if that helps.

Quick triage after looking at the logs and payload:

What I see:
- The failing request sequence shows: primary model (m-redwood-xl) served request a, then under higher concurrency the router selects fallback (m-redwood-xl-quant) for request b. The two models have different tokenization/decoding defaults which account for the truncated field.
- There's no evidence of KV cache TTL misapplication in the two sample requests — the prefixes differ per session. The surprising part is that the SDK-visible connection id for both requests is the same (client_conn=cn-78f6) which suggests request multiplexing over an existing connection. Multiplexing is fine, but the runtime should still annotate the response with the model version used.

Short-term fixes I recommend:
1) Immediate telemetry addition (runtime): include metadata on every response: {"model_variant":"m-redwood-xl-quant", "routed_from":"primary_pool-3"}. This is non-breaking if included under response.meta.
2) SDK change (non-breaking): expose response.meta in the Node and Python SDKs and include a best-effort 'routed_model' field in the event object for streaming clients.
3) Product/ops ask: make routing decisions log an explicit event to tracing so we can correlate request-id -> route-change.

Dev — can you confirm whether adding response.meta will be a trivial runtime toggle? If so, we can push a temporary flag to the FinSight tenant within 48 hours for triage.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

What we'll do now (agreed action plan):
- Ops/Runtime will turn on a scoped response.meta payload for the FinSight tenant that includes model_variant and routing_pool. Target: 48 hours. (Karthik taking lead.)
- SDK team will add a small documentation blurb this week on 'how to surface response metadata' and a short patch to the Node SDK to expose meta in streaming callbacks. Target: 7 days. (Dev to own.)
- Sales Eng (Lauren/Marissa) will run a short verification window with FinSight where they replay the failing payloads and validate model_variant values on each response.

If the scoped metadata shows consistent fallback mapping to variant-B (quant), we'll propose a product roadmap item: 1) a stable response.meta schema for model routing and 2) an opt-in SDK hook (onRouteChange) that emits an event when a request is routed differently than the previous one. That roadmap item will need PM signoff and prioritization.
